assumptions: Day 1 starts an abstract week; visits occur on the first N days of each seven-day block
All configured chores are approved that visit; each habit is a distinct positive habit with one tap/day
Source skills are fixed synthetic tags, reported in activity_skills; absent/locked skills earn no XP
Visits occur at fixed 86400-second intervals; within-visit actions take no modeled time
Care reserves one compatible pair, freezes its installed incubation duration and claims it at the next active visit at or after its deadline, before other activity rewards
End-of-visit care starts the first compatible unowned pair when no egg is pending, opens Coin pouches and feeds all available food to the oldest unevolved pet
Expeditions launch at the end of a visit and are claimed on the next active visit after return

Installed control shares two expedition launches per child/day as well as one per species across potion appearances; an unclaimed trip blocks its species. The separate commitment prototype retains its explicit standalone launch assumptions
New control expedition cosmetic salvage is frozen at launch at at most 10 Coins; old saved trips retain their values. New ordinary duplicate draws use the same ceiling
Challenge bundles keep their egg until every promised grown Base or elemental appearance is owned; eggs promised without a typed potion retain species-wide duplicate salvage

New source events advance every matching challenge; marked distinct-active-day challenges count one qualifying day per occurrence, while other challenge durations remain deadlines rather than minimum waits
Badge and challenge celebration loot does not count as activity, streak credit, daily effort or additional challenge progress
Finite completion draws and authored item quantities fund distinct ingredients and food units; conservative per-target capacity proofs do not promise joint collection of all finite targets
Percentile days are calendar days conditional on completion; unreached trials remain in completion_rate
Finite content counts modeled badges, one-off challenges, obtainable cosmetic identities and companion stages only; it is not total app runway
Remaining finite targets means uncompleted, including missed one-off deadlines; expired unfinished challenges are reported separately and are not future playable content

summary.percentile_basis: Calendar days among trials completing within the horizon; completion_rate includes every trial

audit.message: This forecasts the stated activity/care policy, not full app exhaustion or measured retention.
No private reward offers are read. Coins accumulate; shop affordability and economic balance require a separate spending assumption.
There is no assumed starter pet or guaranteed egg/potion. First hatch depends on the loaded eligible sources and random draws.
First companion is reached in 0% of these trials within the horizon. Inspect ingredient supply and care policy.
First grown companion is reached in 0% of these trials within the horizon. Inspect ingredient supply and care policy.
0 finite targets belong to this modeled source subset. Unmodeled badges and activities are not treated as consumed.

assumptions: This is a hypothetical reduction in new-child Coin income, not a live reward rule. Each trial is an alternative history of one child.

One shared envelope covers direct expedition Coins, expedition cosmetic salvage and all opened Coin pouches, regardless of pouch origin. Other Coin sources, XP and item rolls retain their installed rules.
The envelope resets each simulation calendar day. Unused allowance is not banked; inactive days do not increase the next visit's budget. Null means uncapped and zero omits all included Coins.

Included awards use first-arrival order: expedition claims precede activity and end-of-visit pouch opening. All mounts share the same child's allowance; earlier rewards can leave no allowance for later pouches.

Excess included Coins are omitted, never deferred or owed. Synthetic pouches are still consumed and expedition items retained. This must not be applied retroactively to owned pouches or already committed live expedition loot.
Raw Coins are the included awards encountered within each policy's simulated journey, not a paired uncapped counterfactual. Coin-related progression changes can alter later eligibility and rewards.
Summary and source percentiles are calculated independently across alternative trials; use means or individual trial values to reconcile source totals.
This anonymous experiment changes only new synthetic expedition launches and item promises. No live expedition, reward rule or inventory is changed.
One child's mounts share the daily launch and item allocations. Null means unlimited, zero prevents the selected new commitments, and unused capacity never banks across calendar days.

Requested trips are the configured count after the installed control's shared daily launch allowance. Eligible trips are the smaller of that request and currently available species. Prevented trips are eligible trips withheld by this optional launch quota, not by the installed allowance; unavailable species are reported separately. The standalone commitment prototype retains its explicit launch assumptions.

Nominal item slots are counted only for launched trips. Before drawing loot, the remaining item quota bounds whole slots; each successfully selected item consumes one unit, including pouches and cosmetics later salvaged. Empty eligible pools do not consume item capacity.

Slots requested equal slots promised plus nominal slots withheld by the quota plus permitted slots left unfilled by the eligible pool or Coin commitment policy. Withheld nominal slots are not a counterfactual count of items that would have dropped.

Item-only quotas still allow later Coin-only trips. The Coin commitment policy may also promise zero direct Coins; zero-item, zero-Coin and fully empty trips remain visible rather than being silently skipped.

A saturated day exactly uses an allocation on a relevant eligible opportunity; a limited day actually withholds a trip or nominal slot. Zero allocations do not count idle or no-mount days as saturated. Each day counts at most once per measure.

Frozen loot claims retain their complete item and Coin promises. Claimed and pending items count promised units, including later salvage, not retained inventory. Grandfathered units lack a new-budget reservation marker and are reported separately.
For new-budget promises, slots promised equal claimed items minus grandfathered claimed items plus pending items minus grandfathered pending items. Claims do not consume a later day's allocation.

The unlimited finite denominator removes both optional expedition quotas while retaining the installed allowance, Coin policy and routine. Unavailable targets are excluded acquisition paths, not extra playable runway; this loss cannot be added to the separate Coin-policy comparator.

Authored challenge items, activity drops, boosts and future launch/claim concurrency are outside these expedition slot quotas. This is a design comparison, not a live reservation protocol or retention prediction.
Availability gates are anonymous simulation assumptions. No live challenge, saved goal, reward, calendar or child account is changed.

Current mode ignores valid configured gate rules and retains authored challenge, skill and badge requirements. Milestones adds the selected completed-challenge and skill-level requirements using AND. Milestone plus tenure adds elapsed days since the child's first modeled visit.

Day 1 is start_date and the child's first modeled visit. min_days=14 first permits offering on day 15; inactive days advance this elapsed clock. This is neither active-day tenure nor a consecutive-day streak.

Calendar dates govern new offerings inclusively in both gated modes. An offered challenge keeps its full native duration, even after the offering window closes. Requirements are evaluated once before processing each new fact; past facts are never replayed and a predecessor completion cannot unlock its successor on the same fact.

Visit availability is sampled at the start of each active visit, before that visit's activities. It covers only native-reachable one-off global catalog challenges compatible with the configured routine, including unconfigured challenges. It is not a screen impression, all-app availability, engagement or retention measure.

Waiting visits have no currently available unfinished challenge in that subset and at least one structurally reachable challenge locked by a gate or native badge. Visits after exhaustion or expiration are separate. Inactive dates and blocked challenges are not extra playable content.

Unlock and completion day percentiles are conditional on the trials that reached each event; reached counts include every trial. Unlocked means a native challenge window was actually offered by a new fact, not merely that its conditions became true on an inactive date.

Only one-off global challenges can receive new gates; a repeatable challenge may serve as a predecessor after its first completion. Missed direct-predecessor windows and offerings, and definite native completed-challenge badge dead ends, block descendants rather than generating waiting visits. Other native badge paths remain optimistic; a viable alternative or repeatable path prevents a definite dead-end claim.

The native finite target denominator is retained across gate modes. Structural reachability is optimistic and not a completion forecast; permanently unavailable paths, expired offerings and temporary locks are reported separately. Dates after the horizon and tenure beyond the horizon are temporary locks, not permanent losses.

An authored null duration is an untimed one-time reading milestone. It never expires or restarts, and an unfinished accepted milestone remains available across absences. Its routine-capacity subset is bounded by the scenario horizon without creating a deadline.
challenge_gates.scope: One-off global catalog challenges compatible with this routine; not all app activities.
